verses.text: Justificáti ergo ex fide, pacem habeámus ad Deum per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum:
Per quem et habémus accéssum per fidem in grátiam istam, in qua stamus, et gloriámur in spe glóriæ filiórum Dei.
Non solum autem, sed et gloriámur in tribulatiónibus: sciéntes quod tribulátio patiéntiam operátur:
Patiéntia autem probatiónem, probátio vero spem:
Spes autem non confúndit: quia cáritas Dei diffúsa est in córdibus nostris per Spíritum Sanctum, qui datus est nobis.

responsory.text: Centum quadragínta quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti:
responsory.repeat: Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

responsory.text: Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.
Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

parts.title: Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

verses.text: Being justified therefore by faith, let us have peace with God, through our Lord Jesus Christ:
By whom also we have access through faith into this grace, wherein we stand, and glory in the hope of the glory of the sons of God.
And not only so; but we glory also in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience;
And patience trial; and trial hope;
And hope confoundeth not: because the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us.

responsory.text: A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women.
responsory.repeat: For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

responsory.text: These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.
For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

verses.text: Ut quid enim Christus, cum adhuc infírmi essémus, secúndum tempus, pro ímpiis mórtuus est?
Vix enim pro justo quis móritur: nam pro bono fórsitan quis áudeat mori.
Comméndat autem caritátem suam Deus in nobis: quóniam cum adhuc peccatóres essémus, secúndum tempus,
Christus pro nobis mórtuus est: multo ígitur magis nunc justificáti in sánguine ipsíus, salvi érimus ab ira per ipsum.

responsory.text: Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium:
responsory.repeat: Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

responsory.text: Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium quod habébant, et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes.
Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

verses.text: For why did Christ, when as yet we were weak, according to the time, die for the ungodly?
For scarce for a just man will one die; yet perhaps for a good man some one would dare to die.
But God commendeth his charity towards us; because when as yet we were sinners, according to the time,
Christ died for us; much more therefore, being now justified by his blood, shall we be saved from wrath through him.

responsory.text: I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying:
responsory.repeat: How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

responsory.text: I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:
How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

verses.text: Si enim cum inimíci essémus, reconciliáti sumus Deo per mortem Fílii ejus: multo magis reconciliáti, salvi érimus in vita ipsíus.
Non solum autem: sed et gloriámur in Deo per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, per quem nunc reconciliatiónem accépimus.
Proptérea sicut per unum hóminem peccátum in hunc mundum intrávit, et per peccátum mors, et ita in omnes hómines mors pertránsiit, in quo omnes peccavérunt.

responsory.text: Adoravérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum,
responsory.repeat: Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

responsory.text: Et cecidérunt in conspéctu throni in fácies suas: et benedixérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum.
Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

verses.text: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son; much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life.
And not only so; but also we glory in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received reconciliation.
Wherefore as by one man sin entered into this world, and by sin death; and so death passed upon all men, in whom all have sinned.

responsory.text: They worshipped Him That liveth for ever and ever.
responsory.repeat: And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

responsory.text: And they fell down upon their faces before the throne, and blessed Him That liveth for ever and ever.
And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

parts.title: Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
paragraphs: Nascénte Dómino, luctus cœpit, non cælo, sed mundo: indícitur mátribus lamentátio, Angelis exsultátio, infántibus transmigrátio. Deus est, qui natus est: Innocéntes illi debéntur víctima, qui venit damnáre mundi malítiam. Agnélli debent immolári, quia Agnus futúrus est crucifígi, qui tollit peccáta mundi. Sed oves úlulant matres, quia agnos perdunt sine voce balántes. Grande martýrium, crudéle spectáculum! Exímitur machæra, et nulla intérvenit causa: sola stridet invídia, cum qui natus est, nulli fáciat violéntiam. Sed oves cérnimus matres: quæ super agnos lugent: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus magnus. Pígnora sunt, non crédita, sed creáta; non depósita, sed expósita.

responsory.text: Effudérunt sánguinem Sanctórum velut aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem:
Posuérunt mortália servórum tuórum escas volatílibus cæli, carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.
Et non erat qui sepelíret.

parts.title: From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo.)
paragraphs: The Lord is born, and sorrow breaketh out, not in heaven but on earth; to mothers is proclaimed lamentation, to angels joy, to children translation. God is born, and innocence must be offered up to Him Who cometh to condemn the malice of the world. The Lamb that taketh away the sins of the world is come to be crucified, and the tender flock is brought to the sacrifice. But the mothers will lament over them whose inarticulate bleating is silenced for ever. Let us turn a look on this great martyrdom, this heart-rending sorrow. The sword is drawn, though there is no offence to punish, only jealousy shrieking for Him Who is born, and doth no violence. And here are mothers weeping over the lambs of the flock. In Ramah was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning. which shall be returned hereafter, but they are pledges taken without being given, impounded without being entrusted.

responsory.text: The blood of thy saints have they shed like water round about Jerusalem.
responsory.repeat: And there was none to bury them.

responsory.text: The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.
And there was none to bury them.

paragraphs: Testis est ipsa natura, quæ pugnábat in Mártyres, cum tyránnus jactáret infántes. Mater crines cápitis dissipábat, quæ ornaméntum cápitis amittébat. Quantis modis infántem volébat abscóndere, et ipse se infántulus publicábat! Nesciébat tacére, quia necdum didícerat formidáre. Pugnábat mater, et cárnifex: ille trahébat, illa tenébat. Ad carníficem mater clamábat: Quid séparas a me, quem génui ex me? Uterus génuit, non mansit ille, cum vixit, úbera mea frustra lacte contórquens. Caute portávi, quem a te vídeo manu crudéli jactári. Modo eum effudérunt víscera mea, et tu elídis ad terram.

responsory.text: Isti sunt Sancti, qui passi sunt propter te, Dómine: víndica eos,
Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.
Quia clamant ad te cotídie.

paragraphs: Nature is herself our witness of what the scene must have been when the tyrant dashed the little ones against the stones. The childless mothers tore their hair; those, whose infants had still escaped, strove vainly to hide them, and their very cries betrayed them, too young to have learnt the silence of fear. Sometimes the wretched mother struggled with the executioner, as he dragged the child to which she clung from her arms. The fruit of her body is torn from her breast. Was it for this that her womb bore it, and her paps gave it suck? Had she carried it so tenderly, that the murderer might seize it? It had come of her body only to be dashed against the stones.

responsory.text: These holy ones suffered for thy sake, O Lord take vengeance for them.
responsory.repeat: For day by day they cry unto thee.

responsory.text: Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints which is shed.
For day by day they cry unto thee.

paragraphs: Alia acclamábat mater, cum exáctor latro non compélleret simul occídi cum párvulo matrem: Ut quid me dimíttis inánem? Si culpa est, mea est: si non est crimen, junge mortem, et líbera matrem. Alia dicébat: Quid quǽritis? Unum quǽritis, et multos occíditis, et ad unum, qui unus est, attíngere non potéstis. Alia contra clamábat: Veni jam, veni Salvátor mundi, quámdiu quæréris? Nullum times: vídeat te miles, et nostros non occídat infántes. Miscebátur lamentátio matrum, et ad cælum transíbat oblátio parvulórum.

responsory.text: Isti sunt, qui non inquinavérunt vestiménta sua:
responsory.repeat: Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

responsory.text: Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: vírgines enim sunt.
Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

paragraphs: Sometimes a broken-hearted woman cried to the ruffian to kill her also; wherefore leave her to her childless widowhood? If fault there were, the fault was hers, then why not let her suffer and follow her lost one? Some must have cried out that all were being slain for the sake of One, and that One had escaped. And surely some called for the coming of the Messiah to deliver them. Come, come, O Saviour, how long do we wait for thee? Thou art Almighty come, and save our children. And so the cry of the mother and the sacrifice of her offspring went up together to heaven.

responsory.text: These are they which have not defiled their garments.
responsory.repeat: They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

responsory.text: These are they which were not defiled with women for they are virgins.
They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

parts.title: Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Matthǽum
paragraphs: In illo témpore: Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fuge in Ægýptum, et esto ibi, usque dum dicam tibi. Futúrum est enim, ut Heródes quærat Púerum ad perdéndum eum. Qui consúrgens accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum: et erat ibi usque ad óbitum Heródis: ut adimplerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per Prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum. Tunc Heródes videns, quóniam illúsus esset a Magis, irátus est valde, et mittens occídit omnes púeros, qui erant in Béthlehem et in ómnibus fínibus ejus, a bimátu et infra, secúndum tempus, quod exquisíerat a Magis. Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Jeremíam Prophetam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus: Rachel plorans fílios suos, et nóluit consolári, quia non sunt.

parts.title: Homilía sancti Joánnis Chrysóstomi
parts.source: Ex Hom. 8 in Matth., ante med.
paragraphs: Quæ cum audísset Joseph, nequáquam passus est scándalum, neque dixit: Incérta ista res est, ac prorsus ambígua. Tu paulo ante dicébas, quia salvábit populum suum, et nunc seípsum quidem non potest de perículis liberáre: sed fuga nobis est necessária, et peregrinátio, ac transmigrátio longínqua. Contrária omníno sunt facta promíssis. Sed horum nihil prorsus oppónit: vir enim erat fidélis: neque reversiónis tempus curióse inquírit, quod útique ab Angelo non signáte fúerat expréssum: sed: Esto ibi, inquit, úsquequo dicam tibi.

responsory.text: Cantábant Sancti cánticum novum ante sedem Dei et Agni:
responsory.repeat: Et resonábat terra in voces eórum.

responsory.text: Hi empti sunt ex homínibus primítiæ Deo et Agno, et in ore ipsórum non est invéntum mendácium.
Et resonábat terra in voces eórum.

parts.title: From the Holy Gospel according to Matthew
paragraphs: In that time an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph, saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt: and be there until I shall tell thee. For it will come to pass that Herod will seek the child to destroy him. Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt: and he was there until the death of Herod: That it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son. Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry: and sending killed all the menchildren that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the prophet, saying: A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.

parts.title: Homily by St. John Chrysostom, Patriarch (of Constantinople.)
paragraphs: When Joseph had heard this he was not troubled, neither did he say, This is doubtful, or at least obscure. Thou saidst not long ago, that He shall save His people, and now apparently Himself He cannot save; but we are to flee, and journey far, and dwell in a strange land. thy works belie thy words. But Joseph said none of these things, for he was faithful; neither did he curiously ask of the angel the time of his return, which God was not pleased to show him, but only to send him that word, Be thou there until I bring thee word.

responsory.text: The saints sung a new song before the throne of God and the Lamb.
responsory.repeat: And their voices were echoed on earth.

responsory.text: These were redeemed from among men, being the first-fruits unto God, and to the Lamb, and in their mouth was found no guile.
And their voices were echoed on earth.

paragraphs: Verum ille nec per ista quidem factus est ségnior, sed obedívit libénter, et crédidit, omnes prorsus tribulatiónes cum gáudio sustinéndo. Enim vero miséricors Deus mœstis rebus quædam étiam jucúnda permíscuit. Quod certe in sanctis ómnibus facit, quos neque tribulatiónes, neque jucunditátes sinit habére contínuas: sed tum de advérsis, tum ex prósperis justórum vitam quasi admirábili varietáte contéxit. Quod hic quoque eum fecísse consídera.

responsory.text: Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei quod habébant, et clara voce dicébant:
responsory.repeat: Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

responsory.text: Sub throno Dei omnes Sancti clamant.
Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

paragraphs: He was not slothful, but obeyed cheerfully, and by faith bore all tribulations with joy. God in His mercy mingled some joy with his sorrow, as He doth in all the saints, whom He will have to abide continually neither in sorrow, nor in joy but weaveth their life ever with a strange diversity. And let us consider how He did it here.

responsory.repeat: Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

responsory.text: Under the throne of God all the saints cry aloud
Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints, which is shed.

paragraphs: Vidéndo quippe sanctus Joseph grávidam Vírginem, in conturbatiónem íncidit máximam: sed ádfuit repénte Angelus, timórem prorsus exstínguens. Deínde videns púerum natum, máxima exsultatióne replétus est: sed rursus huic étiam gáudio perículum grande succéssit, cum tota útique cívitas turbarétur, ipse rex fúreret, et ad necem púerum quǽreret. Sed et hunc mœrórem alia rursus lætítia subsecúta est, apparítio vidélicet stellæ, et adorátio Magórum. Post hanc quoque jucunditátem íterum perículum, iterúmque formído. Quærit, inquit, Heródes ánimam púeri, et fúgere necésse est, et in longínqua transíre.

When St. Joseph knew that the Virgin was with child, he was greatly troubled; but forthwith an Angel came to take away his fears. The Lord was born and he rejoiced with exceeding joy; but straightway came the great danger, when all Jerusalem was troubled, the king in great wrath, and murderers seeking the young Child's life. The star shone over Bethlehem, and the wise men came to worship; but Herod sought to slay the Saviour; and they arose, and fled into a far country.

latin.heading: Nonis Januárii Luna vicésima séptima. Anno Dómini 2027
entries: Romæ sancti Telésphori, Papæ et Mártyris; qui, sub Antoníno Pio, post multos labóres, pro Christi confessióne, illústre martýrium duxit.

In Anglia natális sancti Eduárdi, Regis Anglórum et Confessóris; qui virtúte castitátis et grátia miraculórum fuit insígnis. Ejus autem festívitas, ex decréto Innocéntii Papæ Undécimi, tértio Idus Octóbris, quo die sacrum ejus corpus translátum fuit, potíssimum celebrátur.
In Ægýpto commemorátio plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum, qui in Thebáide, sub persecutióne Diocletiáni, divérso tormentórum génere cæsi sunt.
Antiochíæ sancti Simeónis Mónachi, qui, multos annos in colúmna stans vixit, unde et Stylítæ cognómen accépit; cujus vita et conversátio éxstitit admirábilis.
Romæ sanctæ Æmiliánæ Vírginis, amitæ sancti Gregórii Papæ; quæ, vocánte Tharsílla soróre, quæ ad Deum præcésserat, hac ipsa die migrávit ad Dóminum.
Alexandríæ sanctæ Syncléticæ Vírginis, cujus res præcláre gestas sanctus Athanásius monuméntis litterárum commendávit.
latin.closing: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

translation.heading: January 5th 2027, the 27th day of the Moon
entries: The morrow is the Eve of the Epiphany of the Lord, the same day is the Octave of the holy martyr Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.
Upon the same 5th day of January, were born into the better life:
At Rome, the holy Pope Telesphorus, who toiled much for Christ, and under the Emperor Antoninus Pius obtained by his testimony a glorious martyrdom.

In England, the holy King Edward, famous for his gift of chastity and of the power of working miracles. By command of Pope Innocent XI his feast is kept upon the 13th day of October, which is the day of the translation of his sacred body (in the year 1066.)
In Egypt are commemorated many holy martyrs who were slain in the Thebaid in diverse ways, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

At Antioch, the holy monk Simeon, who lived for many years standing upon a pillar, whence he is called Stylitis (from the Greek style, which is being interpreted a pillar), whose life and conversation was wonderful (in the year 459).

At Rome, the holy virgin Emiliana, father's sister to holy Gregory the Great. Her sister Tharsilla, who had gone to God before her, came and called her, and upon the same day she passed hence to be for ever with the Lord (sixth century).
At Alexandria (in the fourth century), holy Syncletica, whose noble acts holy Athanasius hath set before us in his writing.
Upon the same day, the holy virgin Apollinaris (about the year 440).
translation.closing: And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.

Being justified therefore by faith, let us have peace with God, through our Lord Jesus Christ:

Matins · Monday, 4 January 2027

Octave Day of the Holy Innocents

In Octava Ss. Innocentium · Duplex

Read in Latin and English{{listen}}

Lesson I

Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Rom 5:1-5

Being justified therefore by faith, let us have peace with God, through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access through faith into this grace, wherein we stand, and glory in the hope of the glory of the sons of God. And not only so; but we glory also in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience trial; and trial hope; And hope confoundeth not: because the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us.

℟. A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women. * For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

℣. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.

℟. For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

Lesson II

Rom 5:6-9

For why did Christ, when as yet we were weak, according to the time, die for the ungodly? For scarce for a just man will one die; yet perhaps for a good man some one would dare to die. But God commendeth his charity towards us; because when as yet we were sinners, according to the time, Christ died for us; much more therefore, being now justified by his blood, shall we be saved from wrath through him.

℟. I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying: * How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

℣. I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:

℟. How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

Rom 5:10-12

For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son; much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life. From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo.)

1st for Childermas.

The Lord is born, and sorrow breaketh out, not in heaven but on earth; to mothers is proclaimed lamentation, to angels joy, to children translation. God is born, and innocence must be offered up to Him Who cometh to condemn the malice of the world. In Ramah was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning. which shall be returned hereafter, but they are pledges taken without being given, impounded without being entrusted.

℣. The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.

Lesson V

Nature is herself our witness of what the scene must have been when the tyrant dashed the little ones against the stones. De Epístola ad Romános

Lesson from the letter of St. Paul the Apostle to the Romans

Rom 5:1-5

Rom 5:1-5

Justificáti ergo ex fide, pacem habeámus ad Deum per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum: Per quem et habémus accéssum per fidem in grátiam istam, in qua stamus, et gloriámur in spe glóriæ filiórum Dei. Non solum autem, sed et gloriámur in tribulatiónibus: sciéntes quod tribulátio patiéntiam operátur: Patiéntia autem probatiónem, probátio vero spem: Spes autem non confúndit: quia cáritas Dei diffúsa est in córdibus nostris per Spíritum Sanctum, qui datus est nobis.

Being justified therefore by faith, let us have peace with God, through our Lord Jesus Christ: By whom also we have access through faith into this grace, wherein we stand, and glory in the hope of the glory of the sons of God. And not only so; but we glory also in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience trial; and trial hope; And hope confoundeth not: because the charity of God is poured forth in our hearts, by the Holy Ghost, who is given to us.

℟. Centum quadragínta quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: * Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

℟. A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women. * For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

℣. Isti sunt qui venérunt ex magna tribulatióne, et lavérunt stolas suas in sánguine Agni.

℣. These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes in the Blood of the Lamb.

℟. Vírgines enim permansérunt, ídeo regnant cum Deo, et Agnus Dei cum illis.

℟. For they remained virgins; therefore are they kings before God, and the Lamb of God is with them.

Lectio II

Lesson II

Rom 5:6-9

Rom 5:6-9

Ut quid enim Christus, cum adhuc infírmi essémus, secúndum tempus, pro ímpiis mórtuus est? Vix enim pro justo quis móritur: nam pro bono fórsitan quis áudeat mori. Comméndat autem caritátem suam Deus in nobis: quóniam cum adhuc peccatóres essémus, secúndum tempus, Christus pro nobis mórtuus est: multo ígitur magis nunc justificáti in sánguine ipsíus, salvi érimus ab ira per ipsum.

For why did Christ, when as yet we were weak, according to the time, die for the ungodly? For scarce for a just man will one die; yet perhaps for a good man some one would dare to die. But God commendeth his charity towards us; because when as yet we were sinners, according to the time, Christ died for us; much more therefore, being now justified by his blood, shall we be saved from wrath through him.

℟. Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium: * Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

℟. I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying: * How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

℣. Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium quod habébant, et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes.

℣. I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:

℟. Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

℟. How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

Lectio III

Lesson III

Rom 5:10-12

Rom 5:10-12

Si enim cum inimíci essémus, reconciliáti sumus Deo per mortem Fílii ejus: multo magis reconciliáti, salvi érimus in vita ipsíus. Non solum autem: sed et gloriámur in Deo per Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, per quem nunc reconciliatiónem accépimus. Proptérea sicut per unum hóminem peccátum in hunc mundum intrávit, et per peccátum mors, et ita in omnes hómines mors pertránsiit, in quo omnes peccavérunt.

And not only so; but also we glory in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received reconciliation. Wherefore as by one man sin entered into this world, and by sin death; and so death passed upon all men, in whom all have sinned.

℟. Adoravérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum, * Mitténtes corónas suas ante thronum Dómini Dei sui.

℟. They worshipped Him That liveth for ever and ever. * And cast their crowns before the throne of the Lord their God.

℣. Et cecidérunt in conspéctu throni in fácies suas: et benedixérunt vivéntem in sǽcula sæculórum.

Sermo sancti Augustíni Epíscopi

From the Sermons of St. Augustine, Bishop (of Hippo.)

Sermo 1 de Innocentibus

1st for Childermas.

Nascénte Dómino, luctus cœpit, non cælo, sed mundo: indícitur mátribus lamentátio, Angelis exsultátio, infántibus transmigrátio. Deus est, qui natus est: Innocéntes illi debéntur víctima, qui venit damnáre mundi malítiam. Agnélli debent immolári, quia Agnus futúrus est crucifígi, qui tollit peccáta mundi. Sed oves úlulant matres, quia agnos perdunt sine voce balántes. Grande martýrium, crudéle spectáculum! Exímitur machæra, et nulla intérvenit causa: sola stridet invídia, cum qui natus est, nulli fáciat violéntiam. Sed oves cérnimus matres: quæ super agnos lugent: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus magnus. Pígnora sunt, non crédita, sed creáta; non depósita, sed expósita.

The Lord is born, and sorrow breaketh out, not in heaven but on earth; to mothers is proclaimed lamentation, to angels joy, to children translation. God is born, and innocence must be offered up to Him Who cometh to condemn the malice of the world. The Lamb that taketh away the sins of the world is come to be crucified, and the tender flock is brought to the sacrifice. But the mothers will lament over them whose inarticulate bleating is silenced for ever. Let us turn a look on this great martyrdom, this heart-rending sorrow. The sword is drawn, though there is no offence to punish, only jealousy shrieking for Him Who is born, and doth no violence. And here are mothers weeping over the lambs of the flock. In Ramah was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning. which shall be returned hereafter, but they are pledges taken without being given, impounded without being entrusted.

℟. Effudérunt sánguinem Sanctórum velut aquam in circúitu Jerúsalem: * Et non erat qui sepelíret.

℟. The blood of thy saints have they shed like water round about Jerusalem. * And there was none to bury them.

℣. Posuérunt mortália servórum tuórum escas volatílibus cæli, carnes sanctórum tuórum béstiis terræ.

℣. The dead bodies of thy servants have they given to be meat unto the fowls of the air, the flesh of thy saints unto the beasts of the earth.

℟. Et non erat qui sepelíret.

℟. And there was none to bury them.

Lectio V

Lesson V

Testis est ipsa natura, quæ pugnábat in Mártyres, cum tyránnus jactáret infántes. Mater crines cápitis dissipábat, quæ ornaméntum cápitis amittébat. Quantis modis infántem volébat abscóndere, et ipse se infántulus publicábat! Nesciébat tacére, quia necdum didícerat formidáre. Pugnábat mater, et cárnifex: ille trahébat, illa tenébat. Ad carníficem mater clamábat: Quid séparas a me, quem génui ex me? Uterus génuit, non mansit ille, cum vixit, úbera mea frustra lacte contórquens. Caute portávi, quem a te vídeo manu crudéli jactári. Modo eum effudérunt víscera mea, et tu elídis ad terram.

Nature is herself our witness of what the scene must have been when the tyrant dashed the little ones against the stones. The childless mothers tore their hair; those, whose infants had still escaped, strove vainly to hide them, and their very cries betrayed them, too young to have learnt the silence of fear. Sometimes the wretched mother struggled with the executioner, as he dragged the child to which she clung from her arms. The fruit of her body is torn from her breast. Was it for this that her womb bore it, and her paps gave it suck? Had she carried it so tenderly, that the murderer might seize it? It had come of her body only to be dashed against the stones.

℟. Isti sunt Sancti, qui passi sunt propter te, Dómine: víndica eos, * Quia clamant ad te cotídie.

℟. These holy ones suffered for thy sake, O Lord take vengeance for them. * For day by day they cry unto thee.

℣. Víndica, Dómine, sánguinem Sanctórum tuórum, qui effúsus est.

℣. Avenge, O Lord, the blood of thy saints which is shed.

℟. Quia clamant ad te cotídie.

℟. For day by day they cry unto thee.

Lectio VI

Lesson VI

Alia acclamábat mater, cum exáctor latro non compélleret simul occídi cum párvulo matrem: Ut quid me dimíttis inánem? Si culpa est, mea est: si non est crimen, junge mortem, et líbera matrem. Alia dicébat: Quid quǽritis? Unum quǽritis, et multos occíditis, et ad unum, qui unus est, attíngere non potéstis. Alia contra clamábat: Veni jam, veni Salvátor mundi, quámdiu quæréris? Nullum times: vídeat te miles, et nostros non occídat infántes. Miscebátur lamentátio matrum, et ad cælum transíbat oblátio parvulórum.

Sometimes a broken-hearted woman cried to the ruffian to kill her also; wherefore leave her to her childless widowhood? If fault there were, the fault was hers, then why not let her suffer and follow her lost one? Some must have cried out that all were being slain for the sake of One, and that One had escaped. And surely some called for the coming of the Messiah to deliver them. Come, come, O Saviour, how long do we wait for thee? Thou art Almighty come, and save our children. And so the cry of the mother and the sacrifice of her offspring went up together to heaven.

℟. Isti sunt, qui non inquinavérunt vestiménta sua: * Ambulábunt mecum in albis, quia digni sunt.

℟. These are they which have not defiled their garments. * They shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.

℣. Hi sunt, qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti: vírgines enim sunt.

℣. These are they which were not defiled with women for they are virgins.

Matt 2:13-18

In illo témpore: Angelus Dómini appáruit in somnis Joseph, dicens: Surge, et áccipe Púerum et Matrem ejus, et fuge in Ægýptum, et esto ibi, usque dum dicam tibi. Futúrum est enim, ut Heródes quærat Púerum ad perdéndum eum. Qui consúrgens accépit Púerum et Matrem ejus nocte, et secéssit in Ægýptum: et erat ibi usque ad óbitum Heródis: ut adimplerétur quod dictum est a Dómino per Prophétam dicéntem: Ex Ægýpto vocávi Fílium meum. Tunc Heródes videns, quóniam illúsus esset a Magis, irátus est valde, et mittens occídit omnes púeros, qui erant in Béthlehem et in ómnibus fínibus ejus, a bimátu et infra, secúndum tempus, quod exquisíerat a Magis. Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Jeremíam Prophetam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus: Rachel plorans fílios suos, et nóluit consolári, quia non sunt.

In that time an angel of the Lord appeared in sleep to Joseph, saying: Arise, and take the child and his mother, and fly into Egypt: and be there until I shall tell thee. For it will come to pass that Herod will seek the child to destroy him. Who arose, and took the child and his mother by night, and retired into Egypt: and he was there until the death of Herod: That it might be fulfilled which the Lord spoke by the prophet, saying: Out of Egypt have I called my son. Then Herod perceiving that he was deluded by the wise men, was exceeding angry: and sending killed all the menchildren that were in Bethlehem, and in all the borders thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired of the wise men. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the prophet, saying: A voice in Rama was heard, lamentation and great mourning; Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not.

8th on Matthew.

Quæ cum audísset Joseph, nequáquam passus est scándalum, neque dixit: Incérta ista res est, ac prorsus ambígua. Tu paulo ante dicébas, quia salvábit populum suum, et nunc seípsum quidem non potest de perículis liberáre: sed fuga nobis est necessária, et peregrinátio, ac transmigrátio longínqua. Contrária omníno sunt facta promíssis. Sed horum nihil prorsus oppónit: vir enim erat fidélis: neque reversiónis tempus curióse inquírit, quod útique ab Angelo non signáte fúerat expréssum: sed: Esto ibi, inquit, úsquequo dicam tibi.

When Joseph had heard this he was not troubled, neither did he say, This is doubtful, or at least obscure. Thou saidst not long ago, that He shall save His people, and now apparently Himself He cannot save; but we are to flee, and journey far, and dwell in a strange land. thy works belie thy words. But Joseph said none of these things, for he was faithful; neither did he curiously ask of the angel the time of his return, which God was not pleased to show him, but only to send him that word, Be thou there until I bring thee word.

Verum ille nec per ista quidem factus est ségnior, sed obedívit libénter, et crédidit, omnes prorsus tribulatiónes cum gáudio sustinéndo. Enim vero miséricors Deus mœstis rebus quædam étiam jucúnda permíscuit. Quod certe in sanctis ómnibus facit, quos neque tribulatiónes, neque jucunditátes sinit habére contínuas: sed tum de advérsis, tum ex prósperis justórum vitam quasi admirábili varietáte contéxit. Quod hic quoque eum fecísse consídera.

He was not slothful, but obeyed cheerfully, and by faith bore all tribulations with joy. God in His mercy mingled some joy with his sorrow, as He doth in all the saints, whom He will have to abide continually neither in sorrow, nor in joy but weaveth their life ever with a strange diversity. And let us consider how He did it here.

Lesson IX

Vidéndo quippe sanctus Joseph grávidam Vírginem, in conturbatiónem íncidit máximam: sed ádfuit repénte Angelus, timórem prorsus exstínguens. Deínde videns púerum natum, máxima exsultatióne replétus est: sed rursus huic étiam gáudio perículum grande succéssit, cum tota útique cívitas turbarétur, ipse rex fúreret, et ad necem púerum quǽreret. Sed et hunc mœrórem alia rursus lætítia subsecúta est, apparítio vidélicet stellæ, et adorátio Magórum. Post hanc quoque jucunditátem íterum perículum, iterúmque formído. Quærit, inquit, Heródes ánimam púeri, et fúgere necésse est, et in longínqua transíre.

When St. Joseph knew that the Virgin was with child, he was greatly troubled; but forthwith an Angel came to take away his fears. The Lord was born and he rejoiced with exceeding joy; but straightway came the great danger, when all Jerusalem was troubled, the king in great wrath, and murderers seeking the young Child's life. The star shone over Bethlehem, and the wise men came to worship; but Herod sought to slay the Saviour; and they arose, and fled into a far country.

The morrow is the Eve of the Epiphany of the Lord, the same day is the Octave of the holy martyr Thomas, Archbishop of Canterbury.

Upon the same 5th day of January, were born into the better life:

At Rome, the holy Pope Telesphorus, who toiled much for Christ, and under the Emperor Antoninus Pius obtained by his testimony a glorious martyrdom.

In England, the holy King Edward, famous for his gift of chastity and of the power of working miracles. By command of Pope Innocent XI his feast is kept upon the 13th day of October, which is the day of the translation of his sacred body (in the year 1066.)

In Egypt are commemorated many holy martyrs who were slain in the Thebaid in diverse ways, in the persecution under the Emperor Diocletian.

At Rome, the holy virgin Emiliana, father's sister to holy Gregory the Great. Her sister Tharsilla, who had gone to God before her, came and called her, and upon the same day she passed hence to be for ever with the Lord (sixth century).
